## Closing as a duplicate of e7a9

Same underlying defect: the ticket store accepts secret-bearing event bodies at the write
boundary. e4f4 and e7a9 were filed about 8 minutes apart with no link between them, and
would otherwise have had two agents independently build the same screen.

e7a9 is kept as the canonical ticket because it carries the broader fix plan (the pattern
list, the benign-fixture regression cases from jira-reb-687, and the push-diagnostics AC
that e4f4 lacks).

Nothing is lost: this ticket's two ACs with no counterpart in e7a9 have been folded into
e7a9's Acceptance Criteria -- documenting the shell command-substitution hazard for agents,
and recording the incident with its blast radius including that the only control which
stopped the leak was GitHub push protection, outside this project.

Note this is NOT resolved by the rotation and purge. The preventive write-time guard does
not exist in any form today: a comment body containing a live token would still be
accepted, signed, committed and pushed, and would again wedge the tickets branch. That work
remains open on e7a9.

Linked e4f4 -duplicates-> e7a9.
